subject: Pilot → Committed: support-pack conversion and discount scope
messages:
From: Sarah Meyer <sarah.meyer@pawprint.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-12T09:23:00-08:00
Subject: Next steps on pilot -> committed support package

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the excellent onboarding; the pilot telemetry looks solid. We're ready to discuss converting our pilot to a 12-month committed agreement, and a few specific asks came up from Ops and Finance:

- Can you confirm the uptime tiers and how credits are calculated for partial-month incidents?
- We need a 24/7 escalation lane (including weekend on-call) for P1s during our Black Friday window—what's the delta vs standard business-hours coverage?
- Pricing: our CFO is pushing for a meaningful first-year discount given our volume projection; what levers do you have (commitment, multi-region opt-in, annual payment)?

Also, curious if you can include a short runbook add-on (hourly retainer vs per-incident) in the same SOW.

Appreciate a short bullets reply so we can circulate internally.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Meyer
Head of Infrastructure
PawPrint Analytics

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Meyer <sarah.meyer@pawprint.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-12T11:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Next steps on pilot -> committed support package

Hi Sarah — great to hear you want to move forward. Quick answers up front, then I can send a formal SOW: 

- Uptime tiers: we offer Standard (99.5%), Assured (99.9%), and Enterprise (99.95%). Credits are pro-rated monthly based on total downtime minutes against the SLA band; for partial-month incidents we calculate the percentage of the month impacted and apply the credit slab for that tier — I can attach the calculation table.
- Escalation coverage: business-hours (Mon–Fri, 9–5 PT) is included for Standard. 24/7 P1 coverage is available as an add-on (flat monthly uplift + guaranteed on-call roster) or as a seasonal overlay (daily surcharge during defined windows like Black Friday). Typical uplift for continuous 24/7 is 18–25% on top of the base support pack depending on response time target.
- Discount levers: 12+ month commit, up-front annual payment, and multi-region commit (if you want EU + US nodes) are the primary discounts. For a first-year transition from pilot to annual commit we usually provide a one-time onboarding credit and a tiered volume discount (5–12% depending on token/embedding commit).

I've attached a draft SLA and a simple pricing workbook that shows examples. Would you and Tom have availability later this week to align on Black Friday coverage windows?

Thanks —
Soojin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-sla-draft-v2.pdf (SLA draft), ppa-oncall-pricing.xlsx (pricing workbook)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Sarah Meyer <sarah.meyer@pawprint.ai>
Date: 2026-01-13T08:32:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Next steps on pilot -> committed support package

Looping in some pricing guardrails so expectations are clear.

Soojin — quick notes for Sarah/Finance:
- For a 12-month committed plan at forecasted usage, we can provide an introductory commercial concession: 10% off list for year one if PawPrint signs and prepays annually.
- If PawPrint wants the 24/7 P1 lane permanently (not seasonal), the uplift is 20% on the support pack and includes a named on-call rotation plus quarterly incident drills.
- Multi-region commit (US + EU) can add a 4% cross-region discount if both regions are committed at >50% of forecast.
- All credits are cash-equivalent applied to invoices; we can also do a dual-structure where certain operational credits are applied to future support invoices instead.

If you're aiming for more aggressive first-year pricing, we can structure a back-loaded discount that increases with renewal commit. Happy to run the numbers with Connor on the technical impact.

—Ben
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Grant <tom.grant@pawprint.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-14T10:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Next steps on pilot -> committed support package

Thanks Ben/Soojin — that is helpful. A couple follow-ups from our procurement lead: 

1) If we sign mid-quarter, do credits/proration apply to the quarter or is the first invoice prorated monthly? CFO prefers monthly proration.
2) The 10% upfront discount + 20% 24/7 uplift sounds reasonable, but can you do a blended 15% off list for year one if we commit to the multi-region option and a 24/7 seasonal overlay for Black Friday only (vs full-year 24/7)?
3) Also want clarity on SLA measurement window (UTC vs rolling 30-day).

Can you send a version of the SLA with explicit examples (one-pager calculation) so procurement can sign off quicker.

Tom
Director, IT Ops
PawPrint Analytics

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Grant <tom.grant@pawprint.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-15T13:55:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Next steps on pilot -> committed support package

Hi Tom — attaching the SLA draft with example calculations and a short appendix about measurement windows. Short tech clarifications:

- Measurement window: we report uptime on a monthly calendar basis (UTC) and apply credits based on total downtime minutes in that calendar month. For operational transparency we provide a rolling 30-day availability report in the console.
- Proration: invoices are issued monthly; if you sign mid-month we prorate the support pack for the remainder of that calendar month. Credits are calculated on the full calendar month once it closes.
- Black Friday overlay: we support a time-boxed escalation overlay that provides named on-call + 10x triage priority. That overlay is priced as a daily surcharge multiplied by the number of days in the window; if you later convert to full-year 24/7 we credit 50% of the overlay spend toward the first year of the permanent uplift.

See attached: redwood-sla-draft-v2.pdf (with calc table) and ppa-oncall-pricing.xlsx (example workbook). Happy to join a short call to walk procurement through the math.

—Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Meyer <sarah.meyer@pawprint.ai>, Tom Grant <tom.grant@pawprint.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Next steps on pilot -> committed support package

Sarah/Tom — thanks for the thoughtful asks. Proposed commercial construct (short bullets):

- Term: 12 months; start date = execution date; monthly invoicing; first invoice prorated monthly for the partial month.
- Discount: blended 15% off list for year one if PawPrint commits to (a) 12-month term, (b) multi-region commit (US+EU), and (c) season overlay for Black Friday (we price overlay as daily surcharge).
- 24/7 coverage: seasonal overlay for Black Friday (pricing workbook) with credit toward permanent uplift if converted; permanent 24/7 uplift = 20% of support pack.
- SLA credits: monthly calendar (UTC) calculation per attached table; credits applied to invoices as cash-equivalent credits.
- Runbook add-on: we can include a 40-hour retainer at a discounted hourly rate as part of the SOW for onboarding/incident playbook work.

Next step: if this looks acceptable I'll produce an SOW draft and a DocuSign envelope. If PawPrint wants an amplified first-year concession instead of blended discount (e.g., 20% year-one), we can do a conditional renewal incentive that requires renewal commit at 12 months.

Can you confirm procurement's preference on blended 15% vs 20% conditional? If accepted, I'll get the SOW out today.

Thanks —
Soojin
